ashby:cheiron:7b17db14-aeb6-4dbe-a731-99.summary:
Cheiron raised an $11 million seed round led by Menlo Ventures , bringing total funding to $16 million to date, with the backing and strategic support of industry veterans including Moderna co-founder and MIT Institute Professor Robert Langer, former Pfizer Chief Medical Officer Freda Lewis-Hall, Chai Discovery co-founder and CEO Josh Meier, former Starbucks CEO Laxman Narasimhan, and former Apple AI chief John Giannandrea.

Cheiron is building the first AI-native operating system designed to represent an entire drug program as a single connected system. The company’s platform helps biopharma teams represent, reason over, and stress-test the full state of a drug development program, including the claims, evidence, assumptions, risks, decisions, and commitments that determine whether a therapy advances. In less than six months since launch, Cheiron has been adopted by tens of thousands…

sections.title: ■ Company Overview
paras: Cheiron is expanding into pharmaceutical CMC (Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls) teams. CMC governs how a drug is made, tested, and kept consistent across its entire commercial life. The work involves hundreds of regulatory commitments, post-approval changes, and cross-market submissions. Today it runs on documents, spreadsheets, and institutional memory. Cheiron augments manual workflows with a CMC regulatory-specific intelligence and reasoning layer.

Founded in 2024 by Stanford-trained AI researchers. The team includes leaders with combined decades of experience across pharma and biotech. Headquartered in Los Altos, California. We are building and deploying the product now with rapid expansion into global markets.

sections.title: ■ About the Role
paras: You solve product problems end to end. You go deep into how CMC and regulatory teams actually work and how they use our product: how a manufacturing change moves from the plant through QA and regulatory affairs to a filing in each market, who decides what, and where today’s tools fail them. You keep going until you understand the problem better than the brief that named it, then turn it into real user workflows, engineering-ready specs, and data models, settled on paper before a line of code is written.

CMC is a specialized world with its own regulatory frameworks and its own workflows. You do not need to know it coming in. You’ll learn it first-hand, from the regulations and guidance themselves, from customers’ own trackers and filings, and from the people who do the work, with a life sciences team alongside you who own the regulatory rules and check your reasoning. What matters is that you’re the kind of person who immerses until you can reason from first principles.
You’ll work directly with the founders and the product/design, life sciences, and engineering teams.

sections.title: ■ What You'll Do
bullets: Go deep on how our users work: talk to customers, read the trackers, SOPs, and filings they work from, and map each workflow step by step across regulatory affairs, QA, and manufacturing before deciding what to build
Know what customers’ existing systems, such as RIM and QMS, already cover and where they stop, and decide what Cheiron adds on top, including when the honest answer is nothing

Turn what you learn into real user workflows (who does each step, what they need to see, what they decide), then break them into components, define relationships and boundaries with the product team and SMEs, and scope what goes into the build
Write numbered feature stories with acceptance criteria, edge cases, and state transitions that an engineer can pick up cold
Design data models and API contracts against the existing schema; identify what to extend, what to refactor, and what to leave alone
Prototype the workflows you spec, so customers and engineers react to working screens rather than a document
Run specs through review with engineering and the life sciences team before handoff; resolve ambiguity during build rather than letting it travel
Connect proactively with the life sciences team for domain input and approval on regulatory content; know when to engage them and when to move independently

sections.title: ■ What We're Looking For
bullets: 3–6 years in product management at the individual-contributor level
You have found the real problem yourself: you went to the users, learned how the work actually gets done, and changed what got built because of it
You have written build-ready technical specifications (PRDs with data models, API shapes, state diagrams, acceptance criteria) that engineering built from directly
You have shipped at a startup or mid-size company where you had fewer resources and more ambiguity
You can read a codebase, reason about system architecture, and ground a spec in what already exists. You are not writing production code daily, but you understand how production systems are built
Fluent with AI tools like Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent, and you use them to go deeper, not to skip the thinking
Clear, precise writing. A stranger reading your spec can implement it without asking you questions.
When you encounter an unfamiliar domain or system, your instinct is to build a mental model of how it works before deciding what to change

ashby:outtake:89ab9b75-0e65-4a5b-9c8c-19.summary:
Outtake exists to empower and facilitate trust for a digital-first world. Today, impersonation, fraud, AI-driven scams, and identity abuse spread faster than any security team can respond to. So we built something different: an agentic AI platform that proactively detects, monitors, and takes down impersonators, automating protection in hours, not weeks.

Built by ex-Palantir, ex-CTO/founders, and ex-Notion engineers, Outtake is designed for clarity, autonomy, and velocity. Our goal is ambitious: become the trust layer of the modern internet. And we intend to do it with a lean, dense, exceptionally talented team.

Outtake is backed by top-tier investors and operators who believe in our mission and our model. With strong financial footing and a long runway, we prioritize creating an environment where people can do the best work of their careers.

sections.title: The Role
paras: Outtake is looking for a sharp, driven Product Marketing Manager to take the lead on our go-to-market and category-defining efforts. You’ll work directly with the product team to shape how the world understands what we’re building, and why it matters. From competitive insight to messaging, launches to analyst relations, you’ll own the storytelling engine that drives urgency and clarity in a space that’s changing fast.
This isn’t a “check-the-box” marketing role. It’s strategic, scrappy, and high-stakes.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
bullets: Own Outtake’s positioning and messaging, making sure our story is clear, sharp, and consistent across every touchpoint.
Lead market and competitor analysis, surfacing insights that directly shape product direction and GTM plays.
Help define and evolve a category narrative — we’re not just another platform, we’re changing how authenticity is verified online.
Run product launches end-to-end, working across product, sales, customer teams, and leadership.
Equip sales with the right materials, frameworks, and differentiation, built for actual field use.
Lead analyst briefings and relationships to establish Outtake as a category leader.
Partner closely with growth and demand gen to run targeted, high-conviction campaigns.
Build compelling use cases and proof points that turn technical depth into executive-level urgency.

Track record of creating or shifting categories — not just following the market, but pushing it forward.
You’re a strategic thinker and a clear writer — someone who can take a messy idea and turn it into a compelling, usable narrative.
Strong understanding of technical products, and the instincts to translate them into business impact.
Experience building sales enablement and analyst materials that are crisp, confident, and practical.
You move fast, take ownership, and thrive in environments where the playbook is still being written.
You’re collaborative but decisive — able to align cross-functional teams around a shared story.

Owned positioning tear-downs or win/loss programs that led to real GTM changes.
Been the first or only PMM in a startup that went from zero to scale.

ashby:phantom:48fdd46b-c061-4b27-925a-fd.summary: Phantom is on a mission to connect the world to the freedom of open markets. Tens of millions of people all over the world use Phantom to access global markets that never close, including perpetuals, prediction markets, tokenized assets, stablecoins and memes. Phantom users are able to discover the markets that matter and the cultural moments that shape them, building conviction through real-time data and the verified performance of top traders. With self-custody and access to open networks at its core, Phantom lets them control their financial moves in the same app they use to safely store or spend money worldwide.

sections.title: Role Description
paras: Prediction markets are one of Phantom's top priorities, and the category is still wide open. The interfaces everyone uses today are not the end state. As a Senior Product Manager on the Predictions team, you'll shape what trading on real-world events should feel like, from five-minute crypto markets to live sports, politics, and culture.

You'll start with something most prediction products spend years building: more than 20 million people who already hold and trade their money in Phantom, tokens, perps, and stablecoins in the same app. We're looking for someone with the creativity to use that, the judgment to decide what matters, and the drive to see it through without waiting to be asked.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Define how Phantom wins in a competitive market. Build on our funded user base, crypto infrastructure, and existing trading products to make discovering, funding, and trading predictions simpler and more connected.
Own the prediction markets experience end to end, from discovery to payout.
Sweat the design details with our designers. Make trading simpler for someone placing a first prediction and more powerful for someone placing their fiftieth of the day.

Build a team that stays close to traders. Talk to them every week, read support tickets, and dogfood every build. Turn what you learn into roadmap decisions, and make these habits part of how the team works.
Make every trade trustworthy. Own trade execution, position and PnL accuracy, and clear market resolution, so traders can rely on every number on the screen.
Own market discovery and retention. Decide which markets we list and feature, how we surface live events, and how personalization, notifications, and social features give traders reasons to return.
Make the calls. Decide what to build, what to cut, and when something is ready to ship, often with incomplete information, and own the outcome.

Collaborate closely with engineering, design, data, marketing, legal, and our exchange and liquidity partners to ship in a regulated category. Set shared goals and report progress every week, including what isn't working.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: 5+ years as a full-time Product Manager or founder, including a consumer product you owned end to end and grew through measurable improvements in adoption, retention, or revenue.

You trade yourself (prediction markets, perps, crypto, or something more exotic) and have strong opinions about which products do it well. Comfortable reasoning about order books, liquidity, pricing, and settlement.
Original product thinking, with a record of turning what you learned from users into something new that people adopted.
Strong design sensibility. You can point to work where you made something simpler without taking power away from the people who wanted it.
You stay close to users and use AI agents and data to test what you hear, investigate product performance, and measure whether your decisions worked.
You pick up problems without being asked and see them through. You know when to gather more evidence and when to make a call.
A close collaborator. You can lead engineering, design, legal, and marketing without formal authority, and you're technical enough to work through exchange, onchain, and data integrations in detail.

Bonus points if you have:

• Worked at a prediction market, sportsbook, exchange, or brokerage.

sections.title: Why Work With Us
paras: Phantom's journey to becoming a global trading app began with making crypto easier to use. Today, we’re building on that foundation to help people discover the markets that matter, make informed financial moves, and safely store or spend their money worldwide. Joining Phantom means helping shape that next chapter: building products that bring the freedom of open markets to more people.

Make complexity feel simple: Solve meaningful challenges across design, engineering, and user experience to make discovering markets and managing money seamless.

ashby:polymarket:f9107517-12c6-4c43-892d.summary:
Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. We're growing fast, both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire.

paras: The Marketing team at Polymarket is responsible for telling the world what Polymarket is, why it matters, and why trading here is better than reading a poll. We work across growth, brand, comms, and product, and we move fast because the news moves fast.

You'll help shape how we position the product, which audiences we prioritize, how we launch new features and verticals, and how we communicate the value of Polymarket to both existing and prospective traders. Partner closely with Product and Growth leadership to shape product strategy based on customer insights, competitive intelligence, and market trends.
Develop clear positioning and messaging for Polymarket's product, features, market verticals, and key initiatives.
Own go-to-market strategy for major product launches, from defining the audience and narrative through channel strategy, execution, and post-launch analysis.
Build launch frameworks and processes that enable Product, Marketing, Growth, and Comms to move quickly and stay aligned.
Develop deep understanding of Polymarket's users, including why they trade, what drives adoption, and where we can improve conversion and retention.
Translate complex product mechanics into simple, compelling narratives that make sense to both existing traders and new audiences.
Lead competitive research and market intelligence, using those insights to inform positioning and product decisions.

Exceptional at translating complex products or concepts into simple, compelling positioning and messaging.

ashby:ramp:40f43993-21e8-4db1-a9f4-7a3e6.summary:
Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

sections.title: About Ramp
paras: The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Ramp builds software that moves real money, from bill payments and corporate cards to reimbursements, accounting integrations, and travel. Our customers rely on us to keep their operations running: invoices get paid, books get closed, and finance leaders can trust the data behind every decision.

In this role, you will be the person who spots where customers are getting stuck and drives issues to a clear resolution. You will learn a complex product deeply enough to troubleshoot across payments, bank linking, accounting syncs, and card programs, then partner with teams across Engineering, Risk, Product, and Partnerships to get problems solved. This is not script-based support. You will triage, investigate, and make high-signal judgment calls throughout the day.
You will thrive in this role if you are a systems thinker and deeply customer obsessed. Support is the baseline. How you think about improving processes, tools, and outcomes is what sets you apart.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
bullets: Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat.
Diagnose across a broad product surface. Ramp isn't one product — it's payments, cards, travel, accounting integrations, and more. You'll need to understand how they connect and where they break.

Build and shape AI tools, not just use them. Ramp is building AI into CX operations. You'll use AI-powered research tools and proprietary tools like Glass daily, provide direct feedback on what's working, and play an active role in how these tools evolve. You're not just a user — you're a builder. We are all builders at Ramp.

Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler.

sections.title: What You Need
bullets: You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again.
You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement.
You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction.
You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code.
You manage competing priorities without dropping things. When you have 15 open issues across 4 internal teams, nothing falls through.
You write clearly and concisely. You can explain a payment reconciliation issue to a CFO without jargon.
You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there.
You have a demonstrated track record of exceeding key performance standards, including CSAT, QA, and speed-of-service metrics.

In parallel, you will build the commercial foundation that turns our ChemSim work from government-funded R&D workstreams into a product-led business generating durable, recurring revenue from the broader materials and process-chemistry market.

Materials science and industrial chemistry are among the largest and most consequential application areas in applied science. ChemSim spans catalysis, batteries, magnets and alloys, and PFAS replacements: four verticals that underpin refining and downstream oil and gas, commodity and petrochemical production, emissions control, and the energy transition, alongside semiconductor substrates and process chemistry, energy storage, and fine chemical synthesis. Across nearly all of these markets the bottleneck is the same: materials discovery and optimization remain slow, experimental and expensive, and the simulation tools available today answer narrower questions than the ones that actually decide a product or process. This is a once-in-a-career opportunity to shape a category-defining AI platform for materials science

sections.title: From the job description
paras: This is an account management role built around retention, service quality, and problem solving. It’s not a quota-carrying sales job. There’s no cross-sell or upsell target, and no cold outbound. The one exception is re-engaging importers who have gone quiet or moved volume elsewhere, where the goal is to understand what went wrong and win the volume back. What we actually need is someone who can look at an account and a shipment and figure out what is really going on, then drive it to resolution without needing to hand it off.

Own a portfolio of importer accounts . You are the primary relationship owner for a book of existing importers. You are accountable for retention, satisfaction, and the health of the relationship over time.

Diagnose before you escalate . When a client raises an issue, your first job is to determine what kind of issue it is. Is it a rate problem, a service failure, an expectation that was set wrong, or a process that broke internally? The answer determines who needs to be involved and what the fix is. We want you to make that call, not pass it off to someone else.

Review shipments and catch problems early . You should be able to look at a booking and know when something is off before the customer tells you. Rolled bookings, a vessel schedule change that will miss a delivery window, drayage constraints at the port of discharge, a document mismatch that will hold a container at customs. You’ll know when to dig into carrier schedules, customs entry, drayage, or documentation, and when it is normal activity not worth alarming a customer over.
bullets: Direct experience in ocean freight forwarding , NVOCC, or as an importer managing ocean freight. You understand the mechanics of an ocean shipment end to end, from booking and origin cargo receipt through customs clearance and final delivery.
The ability to troubleshoot independently . You form a hypothesis about what went wrong, check it against the data, and act. You don’t need a manager to tell you where to look.
Strong commercial judgment . You know the difference between a concession that’s worth making and one that sets a bad precedent.
Structured thinking . You can take a messy situation with many moving parts, prioritize it, map out next steps, and communicate clearly what happens next and by when.
Clear written communication . Much of this job is explaining a complicated logistics situation to a customer in plain language, quickly.
Comfort in a small company. About 40 people, no large support layer, a lot of ownership.
Experience with a freight forwarding TMS or a modern digital forwarder platform.
Familiarity with customs documentation and entry requirements

You'll design, build and run that system. You'll own the renewal outcome for the business globally and the product and technology that delivers it. You'll lead a small team of builders and the human layer, internal specialists and outsourced partners, that handles what agents can't yet. The data the system runs on: contract, commit burndown and usage data clean enough that agents and people trust it, built with Billing and Finance.
Early-warning signals for consumption risk and commitment shortfall, and what happens when one fires.
The human layer: how internal specialists, outsourced partners and account teams work around the agents, and the measures they're held to.
The next large renewal cycles, run with fewer manual steps per renewal than today.

Executive renewal conversations on the largest and most complex accounts, alongside account teams.

sections.title: Job Description
paras: Renaissance Intelligence brings Math, Literacy, Assessment, MTSS and CFA solutions together in one platform, and the administrator experience is what makes them work as a single product for district and school leaders. As Director, Leader Journeys, you will own that experience across the full Renaissance Intelligence portfolio. You will define the end-to-end workflows leaders use to set up, monitor and act on data from every solution, partner with solution owners and Product Management to make those workflows cohere, and own go-to-market readiness for the admin experience. You will collaborate cross-functionally to build consensus and ensure execution, and represent the needs of administrators across the Renaissance organization.

sections.title: In this role as a Director of Product Management, you will:
bullets: Develop, maintain, and communicate the leader journey vision and strategy across Renaissance Intelligence, partnering closely with Product Management & Solution Leadership to plan roadmaps, drive strategic integrations, and track key initiatives.

Partner with the solution leaders for Math, Literacy, Assessment, MTSS and CFA so each solution's admin capabilities fit one coherent leader experience, and resolve cross-solution gaps and dependencies.
Own go-to-market readiness for the admin experience, partnering with Sales, Enablement, Product Marketing, Customer Success, and Customer Education to bring it to market and align field messaging.

Identify and prioritize gaps in the leader journey that limit the strength of the portfolio, and own living, canonical documentation (journey maps, persona definitions, decisions) so gaps and dependencies are visible to Product, Content, Engineering, GTM, and executive stakeholders, tracked to a decision or resolution.
Define and track success metrics for administrator adoption, engagement, and value, and use them to guide roadmap priorities.
Serve as the subject matter expert for the district and school leader persona in product development and GTM conversations, including demonstrations, training, and integration planning.

Build and sustain relationships with district and school leaders, including superintendents, curriculum and assessment directors, and MTSS coordinators; maintain an ongoing presence with customers and synthesize field signals back to Product, Content, Learning Science, and GTM teams.
Partner with Government Affairs and Sales on the state and district requirements that shape the admin experience, including accountability reporting, data privacy, accessibility, and procurement.

Provider Onboarding owns activation, focused on taking a dietitian, medical provider, or therapist from signed offer to confidently seeing their first patient. This team sets the stage for a successful provider start, and if done right, a provider starts fast, stays longer, and performs better.

As Director of Provider Onboarding , you'll own that function end-to-end, across the team, the operating model, and the systems behind it. This is a rare opportunity to optimize an existing team already onboarding providers at scale (RDs), while creating the 0>1 onboarding approach for new providers. On the RD side, activation has held around flat all year with minimal movement, and needs further investment and focus to structurally change the rate at which providers successfully start. At the same time, you'll build the 0→1 onboarding motion for Nourish Medical and Therapy as we expand beyond dietitians into a full virtual metabolic health clinic.

You'll manage and grow a team of Provider Onboarding Associates, and partner closely with Provider Recruiting upstream, and Provider Strategy and Provider Enablement downstream, and Credentialing, People, and Product throughout. This person will report into our VP of Provider Growth.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities:
bullets: Own provider activation across every provider type: S et the org strategy/vision and lead the team to execute against it, d iagnose where providers stall between signed offer and first patient, and build the system/processes to ensure successful improvement of metrics over time

Build and develop the onboarding team: Hiring and ramping new associates as the team scales, and establishing the performance expectations, coaching cadence, and accountability structure that motivates the team to achieve great outcomes.
Design the operating model and systems: Use our CRM, sequencing, and LMS tooling to automate low-value touchpoints
Stand up onboarding for new provider types: Build the Medical and Therapy motions from scratch and deciding what's shared infrastructure versus provider-type specific
Own the capacity and ROI model: Build headcount and investment plans to drive further activation improvements in 2027 and beyond.

Partner cross-functionally: Across product, recruiting, and ongoing provider strategy, you’ll ensure there are thoughtful handoffs and great product to drive an overarching provider experience that increases overall supply and drives NPS

bullets: You have 8+ years of experience , ideally in a marketplace, provider network, or high-growth startup environment
You've owned a critical funnel metric end-to-end, and know what it takes to structurally improve key funnel metrics

You’ve led teams before and are excellent at people management & driving teams to high performance. You’re results-driven and metrics-oriented, and not afraid of holding people accountable to targets.
You have strong instincts for systems and automation, knowing which human touchpoints to replace with AI automation, and which ones to protect to maintain a delightful provider experience
You're comfortable in the numbers , from cohort analysis to caseload modeling to building the ROI case for your own headcount
You hold a high bar for the provider experience and want to help Nourish be the best place for providers to work
You're energized by ambiguity, moving through roadblocks and challenges to get to a final approach that achieves outcomes

We hire people who find the problem rather than wait for it, decide with incomplete information, and ship.

The handoff to enterprise. Detect when self-serve usage clusters inside a company, build the in-product motions that spread it (invites, shared workspaces, team practice), and route qualified accounts to sales with the context they need to open a conversation.
The experiment system. The roadmap, the instrumentation, and the cadence. You decide what gets tested, you call the results, and you make sure we learn something either way.

We are re-architecting the entire financial system for entrepreneurs. From the first dollar a business earns to how that value compounds, moves, and is ultimately spent in real life. Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, financial operations, all rebuilt from the ground up as a single intelligent system.

sections.title: About Flex
paras: Our customers are affluent business owners with $3M to $200M in revenue. The backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. We are replacing the outdated banks and fragmented tools they are stuck with. The opportunity is a roughly $1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. We are building toward $100B+ in enterprise value by delivering a product that is fundamentally better, not incrementally improved.
Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt.
What we hold ourselves to: mission-critical problems, high bar low ego, speed over comfort, enduring impact.

sections.title: The Role
paras: You will build Flex's payments infrastructure. You will lead our vendor strategy across acquiring, international money movement, and partner banks. You will architect how Flex orchestrates multiple payment providers across bank partners, processors, and international rails into a single elegant customer experience. And you will be the product partner on our transition from operating on partner licenses to operating on our own money transmitter licenses, which is a foundational shift in how Flex works.

This seat requires someone who can hold a serious technical conversation with a Tier 1 bank, who has personally implemented payment rails at meaningful scale, and who can translate vendor selection into clear product decisions. The candidate we want has lived through at least one major payments transition (processor change, license expansion, or rails buildout) and knows what to watch for.

You do not need to be a lawyer. You do need to understand what the operational shift into a forward thinking strategy around money movement means, and be able to communicate the now program, the in-between, and the future program clearly to the rest of the company.
